**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The assignment package here already delivers the substance of our preferred position, and no change-of-control exposure exists:

- **Our assignment rights are protected.** Section 10.2(a)'s prohibition is expressly carved out by Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6. Section 5.3 lets the Depositor pass the Agreement to a merger/consolidation counterparty, a successor to its business, or an Affiliate assignee without Cellco's consent — the affiliate/successor/M&A carve-out the rule demands. The formalities (15-Business-Day assumption agreement, Officer's Certificate, Opinion of Counsel, Rating Agency notice) are successor mechanics, roughly the fallback's "written notice."
- **The restriction is symmetric.** Section 7.6 is the mirror image for Cellco as Servicer, and the residual consent gate in 10.2(a) runs to the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and 66-2/3% of the Controlling Class — investor protection, not a counterparty veto over us.
- **No vendor exit on change of control.** "Change of control" appears nowhere in the document. Cellco has no termination or re-pricing right on a change of control of the Issuer or Depositor; Section 7.1 actually bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer unless legally unable to perform. The Class A Certificateholder's Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption rights (Sections 8.1–8.2) are triggered by pool balance and calendar date, not by any change of control, so they are not walk-away territory.
- **Issuer side confirmed.** Section 2.2 acknowledges the Issuer's assignment and pledge to the Indenture Trustee, and Section 10.2(b) binds permitted successors and assigns. Section 9.2's no-transfer covenant is collateral protection running in our favour, not an assignment restriction on us.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged (minor sub-elements short of preferred): consent under 10.2(a) is not qualified by "not to be unreasonably withheld," and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor. Neither is material here given the consent parties are the trustees and noteholders rather than Cellco.
